name: Camera field of view
title: Camera Field of View Calculator
desc: How much of that landscape will fit in your pictures? Discover it with our camera field of view calculator!

c: focal_length == 0.05  and hasValue(distance) == false and sensors_width == 0.0235 and sensors_height == 0.0156
Onim Example 1: 50mm angle of view — A camera has a 50mm lens with a 23.5 × 15.6 mm sensor. What’s the camera’s angle of view?
focal_length == 0.024  and distance == 10 and sensors_width == 0.0223 and sensors_height == 0.0149
Onim Example 2: 24mm field of view — A camera with a 24mm focal length lens and a 22.3 × 14.9 mm sensor is placed at a distance of 10 m from the subject. What's the camera’s field of view?

How the result is calculated: Identify the focal length f and the sensor dimensions: width and height. Calculate the sensor diagonal: s_diagonal = √(s_width² + s_height²) Apply the angle of view formula to each sensor dimension (width, height, and diagonal): aovᵢ = 2 × arctan(sᵢ / (2 × f))

How the result is calculated: Calculate the sensor diagonal size: s_diagonal = √(s_width² + s_height²) Determine the angle of view for each sensor dimension (horizontal, vertical, and diagonal): aovᵢ = 2 × arctan(sᵢ / (2 × f)) Compute the field of view for each direction: fovᵢ = 2 × tan(aovᵢ / 2) × d
Check our examples: • Example 1 ⧉ – 50mm angle of view • Example 2 ⧉ – 24mm field of view

js: "use strict";omni.define("get_month",function(gap){gap=1-gap/100;var today=new Date;var year_start=new Date(today.getFullYear(),0,1);var year_end=new Date(today.getFullYear()+1,0,1);var work_free_until=new Date(year_start.getTime()+(1-gap)*(year_end.getTime()-year_start.getTime()));return Math.abs(work_free_until.getMonth())});omni.define("get_day",function(gap){gap=1-gap/100;var today=new Date;var year_start=new Date(today.getFullYear(),0,1);var year_end=new Date(today.getFullYear()+1,0,1);var work_free_until=new Date(year_start.getTime()+(1-gap)*(year_end.getTime()-year_start.getTime()));return Math.abs(work_free_until.getDate())});omni.define("get_days",function(gap){gap=1-gap/100;var today=new Date;var year_start=new Date(today.getFullYear(),0,1);var year_end=new Date(today.getFullYear()+1,0,1);var work_free_until=new Date(year_start.getTime()+(1-gap)*(year_end.getTime()-year_start.getTime()));var work_free_days=Math.round((work_free_until-year_start)/86400/1000);return Math.abs(work_free_days)});//# sourceURL=customJs.js

c: Inspired by Bram Stoker's Dracula and Stephen King's Salem's Lot. In 1897 (the year Stoker's novel was first published), the world population was about 1,650 million people. In this scenario we assume only one vampire at the beginning. The vampire attacks a victim that eventually becomes another vampire.

Inspired by Anne Rice's Vampire Chronicles. The author takes us to the year 1791 where the world's population was about 982 million people. Then two vampires appeared. Vampires discretely attack a human being and need victims' permission before turning them into a vampire, so it happens rarely.

Inspired by Stephenie Meyer's Twilight, Charlaine Harris's Southern Vampire or the True Blood TV series. This time, vampires **can coexist with humans. Vampires occasionally attack humans but turning a human into a vampire requires so much effort it rarely happens. On the other hand, vampire slayers hunt vampires for their precious blood.

Damped oscillation - the custom scenario. The current human population is about 7.7 billion, and it's growing by 1% per year. Let's say that vampires are smart and will refrain from killing too many people, because they need a constant source of food. On the other hand, vampire slayers constantly recruit new members. Who will win this war?

Dusk of humanity - the custom scenario. 500 ruthless vampires decided to attack a small, developing city. People realise the incoming danger and create a group of 101 brave vampires slayers to save the city. Vampire slayers certainly need to train new members as the vampire population grows quickly. Is it too late, though?

You're creating your own story! Set the parameters for the three species: humans naturally reproduce and are the primary prey for vampires, vampires can't reproduce like human's, but can turn humans into new vampires, vampire slayers professionally slay vampires and can recruit new members. Try playing with different sets of parameters and see on the chart how the populations changes with time.
